text:
nora: Noticing a jump in funcall parse failures for kestrel-hybrid-int2 (streaming) on canary: +4.2% vs baseline. Mostly mid-object truncation and occasional duplicated punctuation. :confused:

vik: Any concrete examples?

nora: ```
{"task":"charge_account","payload":{"user":42,"amount":9.99,}}
...stream ends...
```

jake: Duplicated comma then cut. Could be early EOS or token swap around punctuation/brace.

vik: Run token-align on 1k samples and grab last-10 logits for truncated cases. Also compare streaming chunk boundaries.

nora: CI-bot please run struct-sanity(500) and token-align(1000) on canary vs float; enable opt-in resume-probe for 10% canary traffic while we investigate.

ci-bot: struct-sanity(500) for kestrel-hybrid-int2 queued. resume-probe enabled for 10% canary. ETA ~2m.

jake: Short-term mitigation: conservative postprocess that strips trailing commas, closes unmatched opens, and marks results as REPAIRED. Add metric repaired_parse_rate and resumed_parse_rate.

vik: Also kick a kv-cache-off canary to rule out cache amplification.

ci-bot: Results ready: kestrel-hybrid-int2 parse_success=91.3%, repaired_success=4.5%, resumed_success=1.8%, final_failure=2.4%. baseline parse_success=95.7%, repaired_success=0.6%, final_failure=3.7%. Full report: /canary/reports/kestrel-hybrid-int2/3301234567.json

nora: Repair/resume helps but raw parse gap ~4.4%. Action items: (1) inspect token-align diffs for punctuation/EOS concentration, (2) run quick quant calibration sweep (try per-channel and small clip), (3) run kv-cache-off canary and collect chunk traces/last logits.

jake: Gate: hold rollout until raw parse within 1% of baseline or we have a robust mitigation that doesn't rely on heavy repair.

nora: I'll coordinate the sweep and post updates. Thanks all :thumbsup:
